In addition to these five projects, additional solar-only options were prioritized based upon return on investment and ability to reduce blue sky energy costs. Economic modeling of all projects included the payback to the City inclusive of federal solar development task credits including applicable Build America, Buy America and low-income enhancements. Duluth’s CERP also highlighted the minimum resilience standards that were developed and ongoing partnership approaches to develop actionable assistance programs for building individual power resilience. During the second half of the F3 project, the process and resources used to develop Duluth’s CERP were developed into the Community Resilience Planning Toolkit (Toolkit) to be used by other capacity-limited Midwest communities. Three communities, Rapid City, South Dakota, and Morehead and Maplewood, Minnesota, entered into 20 memorandums of understanding with the City of Duluth to test aspects of the planning process and provide feedback on the final toolkit. The Toolkit focuses on cold-climate communities and assists municipal staff and community organizations on pairing solar and storage asset planning with community- based approaches. Written to enable community champions to succeed in planning efforts, the toolkit addresses team building approaches, stakeholder recruitment, development of Critical Infrastructure Teams and Community Stakeholder Groups, community vulnerability assessments, grid reliability metrics, scenario creation and tabletop exercise development, community-based research recommendations, and asset assessment methodologies. The toolkit provides a quicker on-ramp to community resilience planning than would generally be possible for government employees and community members. Important resources that accompany the Toolkit as appendices are Definitions, Duluth and Morehead’s Tabletop Scenarios, the Community Service Tabletop Persona Development Tool, Duluth’s 2-Year Community Research Plan, the Solar Siting Rubric, Solar Site Master List Example, Community Resilience Plan Outline, and Duluth’s Minimum Resilience Standards. Significant Accomplishments and Conclusions The F3 project advances the field of resilience planning by implementing a novel integration of traditional top-down asset-based approaches with community-based bottom-up methodologies. It provides a structure and resources to guide capacity- limited communities toward establishment of cross-sectoral community resilience plans centered on governmental solar and storage projects augmented with individual or community-based actions that can be taken to lessen negative impacts during grid outages. The established toolkit provides a community resilience plan outline that can, at its most basic, document the process and results for a community based upon the F3 approach, however, it has further resources for communities that have the capacity to expand the plan into deeper exploration of environmental disparities, broader non-energy focused resilience (e.g. water management, etc.), or policies. The asset-based approach, detailed in the toolkit, assists governmental planners, sustainability officers, and facility managers by providing a methodology for limiting financial exposure by right-sizing initial investigations, engaging with the public to surface any opposition or preferred options, and only investing in engineering and design for pre-vetted and prioritized projects.
